newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - August 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - August 1.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

In the wake of last week's loss to New Zealand, Australian rugby union officials are reconsidering the future of Wallaby coach Greg Smith. Smith could be replaced before the end-of-year Wallaby tour of Argentina and Britain if the team's performance does not improve. Page 20.

Australian under-23 basketball coach Ian Stacker has warned his team not to focus on performing well for American talent scouts at the under-23 world championship being held in Melbourne. Stacker wants the team to concentrate on its own performance, withit being a favourite for the gold medal. Page 19.

Australian tennis player Michael Tebbut has defeated fellow Australian and David Cup champion Pat Rafter 6-7, 6-4, 6-4 in the Canadian Open yesterday. The win advances Tebbut to the third round of the competition. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The chairman and chief executives of the 12 Australian Rugby League (ARL) clubs met in Sydney yesterday to discuss the future of the competition. Prominent on the agenda was a possible reduction in the number of ARL teams in order to promote a united cometition with other football leagues. Page 46.

The Australian 1997 Women's National Basketball League competition has seen the Sydney Flames emerge as the dominant team. They currently sit on top of the league ladder with a 17-0 win record. If the team wins tomorrow's match against Adelaide Lightnin, they will have completed their first regular undefeated season in 17 years. Page 45.

Sprinter Cathy Freeman has emerged as Australia's best gold medal chance at the world athletics championships starting this Saturday in Athens. The 400 metres Olympic silver medalist is currently ranked World No 1 in the event and has high hopes of confiming her status. Page 44.
THE AGE

Australian Football League (AFL) chief executive Wayne Jackson yesterday agreed to meet with the 16 AFL club presidents, who are concerned about the AFL's decision to link the sale of its television rights to the Docklands stadium development in Melbourne. Page D3.

Australia's premier horse race, the Melbourne Cup, advanced a stage further yesterday in its quest to become a world class event with Queen Elizabeth making her first Southern Hemisphere entry with Arabian Story. The Queen's horse is one of the 25 overses entries in the A$2.2 million race. Page D2.

Australian Cricket captain Mark Taylor's back injury has worsened and he has been forced to withdraw from tomorrow's match against county team Somerset. Team physio Errol Alcott says he should be fit to participate in next week's fifth Test at Trent Bride. Page D5.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League team the Western Bulldogs have dropped five players following their recent 97 point loss to the Sydney Swans. The Western Bulldogs have lost their last three games and must win their next match in order to remain in the top eight of the competition ladder. Page 112.

Leading Australian racehorse trainer Gerald Ryan, who last year withdraw from the industry amidst allegation of sexual misconduct, is attempting to revive his career. Ryan yesterday made an official application for a new Victorian training permit. Page 10.

Australian Football League (AFL) players charged with racial abuse will be allowed legal representation at the AFL tribunal. The League has changed its racial vilification rules with players and officials now facing fines of up to A$10,000 for breaking confidentiality agreements. Page 110.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Rebel competition Super League could be forced to abandon its name if it wishes to merge with the Australian Rugby League (ARL) in a national competition next year. ARL sources confirmed last night that any merged national competition would not be called Super League. Page 118.

Netball player Karen Miller has been unexpectedly thrust back into competition, having to fill in for Sydney Sandpipers team-mate Carissa Tombs who injured her knee before the inaugural national netball league, the Commonwealth Bank Trophy. Miller has been sidelined with injuries for most of this year's season. Page 118.

Australian Football League team the Sydney Swans have been saved from difficulties after player Jason Mooney passing his medical test last night. Mooney's fitness was important, as regular ruckman Greg Stafford has been ordered out of tomorrow's match aginst Melbourne because of a knee injury. Page 116.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
